transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
My mind just doesn’t seem to work the way it used to—I can’t think straight or make simple decisions anymore. It has gotten to the point where even basic daily tasks feel completely overwhelming.

Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling persistently sad or hopeless, or are these difficulties with thinking and decision-making occurring even when you feel relatively stable in your mood?

Most days I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling that just sits with me all day, and it has been like that for over a year now. But early on, before the sadness really took over, I had a few weeks where I still enjoyed my quilting group, even though my mind was already getting jumbled and I was convinced the hospital staff were working against my sister.
During those weeks when you felt the hospital staff were working against your sister, did you also hear voices or see things that other people said weren't there?

No, I didn't hear any voices or see anything unusual like that. I just felt very strongly that the doctors and nurses were working against us and changing her charts, but I didn't have any of those other experiences.

When you felt the hospital staff were working against your sister, were you experiencing other symptoms like a significant decrease in your need for sleep, feeling unusually energetic, or racing thoughts?

No, it was actually the exact opposite of that. I felt completely slowed down, like I was moving underwater, and my mind felt like it was filled with cotton. I didn't have any extra energy or racing thoughts at all.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological condition, such as a head injury, stroke, or a chronic medical illness that might affect your brain function?
No, I don't think I've ever been diagnosed with any neurological conditions, strokes, or head injuries. I really just experience the typical aches and pains of getting older, but nothing like that.
When you felt the hospital staff were working against your sister, was that belief present even during times when your mood was not feeling heavy or hopeless?

Yes, early on there was a period of a few weeks where I still felt okay mood-wise and was enjoying my quilting circle. Even though I wasn't feeling sad yet, I was already absolutely convinced that the hospital staff were working against us and changing my sister's charts.
Has this firm belief about the hospital staff persisted throughout this past year, or did it resolve completely once you started feeling this persistent sadness?

No, those suspicious thoughts didn't go away at all when the sadness started. Even though that belief started first when I was still enjoying my quilting, once the heavy, hopeless mood set in, the two things got completely tangled together and have both persisted for over a year now.
Besides the belief about the hospital staff, have you held any other strong, fixed beliefs that others might find difficult to believe, or is this specific concern the only one that has persisted?

No, that is really the only worry of that kind I've had. I haven't had any other suspicious or unusual thoughts about other people or situations in my life. This specific concern about the hospital staff is the only one that has been weighing so heavily on my mind.

Since that initial period, has the belief about the hospital staff remained the primary focus of your concerns, or have you experienced periods where your mood symptoms were so severe that they caused you to lose touch with reality in other ways?

Yes, that belief about the hospital staff has remained the main focus, and I haven't lost touch with reality in any other ways. For most of this past year and a half, those suspicious thoughts and my heavy, depressed mood have been closely tangled together, even though the suspicion actually started first before the deep sadness fully set in.

During the times when your mood has been at its absolute lowest, have you ever felt that your thoughts or beliefs about the hospital staff became so intense that they dominated your mind to the point where you couldn't function or care for yourself?

Yes, during those lowest times, the heavy sadness and my worries about the hospital were completely tangled together and made it impossible to function. I felt so overwhelmed and foggy that I fell behind on my bills, missed my sister's medication refills, and would just freeze up when trying to do simple tasks. It felt like I couldn't manage my daily life at all.

Have you ever experienced any other symptoms, such as disorganized speech or a significant decline in your ability to take care of your personal hygiene and daily responsibilities, during the times you felt suspicious?

Yes, my words get terribly jumbled now—I'll start talking about the drive to the doctor, jump to my quilting group, and then completely forget what we were even discussing. My daily life has really suffered too, because I often just wander aimlessly around the house or freeze up when trying to pay bills or manage my sister's medications.
Have you noticed any problems with your short-term memory, such as frequently forgetting recent conversations or where you placed your belongings, aside from the difficulty concentrating?

Yes, I definitely struggle with those kinds of lapses, and it's quite embarrassing. I often find myself wandering from room to room, picking things up and putting them down, or just standing in the hallway completely forgetting why I went there in the first place. I even lost track of my thoughts so badly recently that I forgot an important medication refill for my sister, which really scared and overwhelmed me.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, such as tremors, stiffness, or changes in the way you walk, that have developed alongside these memory and thinking difficulties?

Yes, I've noticed a real physical slowness lately. My family says I move and talk like I'm underwater, and just getting up from a chair or walking to the kitchen takes me much longer than it used to. It really feels like my body is dragging behind my mind.
Has your doctor ever mentioned any specific medical findings from blood tests, brain scans, or physical exams that might explain these physical and mental changes?

No, I don't recall any abnormal findings from the blood tests or scans my doctor ran. My primary care doctor said they couldn't find a physical cause for how I've been feeling, which is why they referred me here for this psychiatric assessment.

Has there been a noticeable, gradual decline in your ability to remember recent events or manage complex tasks over these past few years, beyond just the times when you feel particularly sad or suspicious?

I've definitely had a lot of trouble managing complex tasks lately, like keeping up with my bills, tracking appointments, and organizing my sister's medications because of this mental fogginess. However, this hasn't been a slow decline over many years; it all started about a year and a half ago, right around the time my sister became ill and I began feeling so overwhelmed, depressed, and suspicious of her doctors.
Have you noticed any subtle changes in your vision, such as seeing shadows or patterns that aren't there, or perhaps having difficulty judging distances when walking?
No, I haven't noticed any changes in my vision like seeing shadows or patterns that aren't there. I also don't have any trouble judging distances when I'm walking around.
